technical.lead: Claude hits GA in Microsoft Foundry on Azure-hosted GB300
technical.body: Anthropic and Microsoft moved Claude from preview to general availability inside Microsoft Foundry on June 29, exposing Claude Opus 4.8 and Haiku 4.5 through the Messages API with prompt caching and extended thinking. The generally available "hosted on Azure" tier runs end-to-end on Azure infrastructure under enterprise identity, networking, billing and governance controls, with a single consolidated invoice and Microsoft Enterprise Agreement integration, while the "hosted on Anthropic infrastructure" tier stays in preview.

technical.lead: vLLM v0.24.0 ships quantized-default Model Runner V2
technical.body: The dominant open-source inference server cut vLLM v0.24.0, landing 571 commits from 256 contributors. Model Runner V2 now supports quantized models by default, a multi-tier KV-cache offloading path adds an object-store secondary tier for spilling cache beyond GPU memory, DeepSeek-V4 got a sparse index cache and prefill chunk-planning pass, and DeepEP v2 was integrated for MoE expert parallelism. Kernels claim a 180-290% SM90 CUTLASS FP8 speedup via swap_ab, and the Rust frontend matured with auth, CORS, tokenization endpoints and a unified tool-call/reasoning streaming parser.

technical.lead: WorldEvolver evolves world models at inference for agent planning
technical.body: A June 29 arXiv paper, "Self-Evolving World Models for LLM Agent Planning" by Xuan Zhang, Wenxuan Zhang, See-Kiong Ng and Yang Deng, targets agents that plan badly because they predict action consequences badly. The WorldEvolver framework couples episodic memory, a semantic memory that distills explicit rules from prediction errors, and selective foresight that filters unreliable predictions before the planner sees them. The world model keeps evolving during deployment while the core agent stays frozen, adapting at inference without retraining. The authors report top prediction accuracy across three backbones and higher task-success rates than competing world-model baselines.

technical.lead: AI Engineer World's Fair mid-run; chip and security dates locked
technical.body: The AI Engineer World's Fair is mid-run at Moscone West in San Francisco (June 29 through July 2; ~29 tracks, ~300 speakers, 6,000+ attendees), with the Autoresearch keynote on July 1 and Harness Engineering on July 2. On the chip track, AMD's Advancing AI 2026 is July 22-23 and Hot Chips 2026 runs August 23-25 at Stanford. On security, SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit is August 11-12 at the Ritz-Carlton Half Moon Bay, ahead of Black Hat USA and DEF CON 34 in early August.

technical.lead: Azure-hosted Claude tier runs on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72
technical.body: The infrastructure layer is the differentiator behind the Foundry launch: the Azure-hosted Claude tier runs on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems with Quantum-X800 InfiniBand networking, with NVIDIA pitching the GB300's inference efficiency as a total-cost-of-ownership reducer and pairing the rollout with its Secure Agent Workspace reference design for autonomous, domain-specific agents. A frontier lab's flagship models now sit alongside the hyperscaler's own catalog on the hyperscaler's silicon, narrowing the gap between calling the lab's API and deploying inside your cloud tenant.
